name.en-US: The Eighteen Martyrs of Saragossa and St. Engratia
name.pt-BR: Os Dezoito Mártires de Saragoça e Santa Engrácia

prayerExcerpt.en-US: If we persevere in these, Paradise is ours.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Se nelas perseverarmos, o Paraíso é nosso.

meta.face: Two clearly different people of Roman Hispania with warm, light-olive skin. ENGRATIA (left): a young woman of about twenty with a LONG, OVAL face and a FIRM, SQUARE-TIPPED chin — a smooth, high forehead, a STRONG, STRAIGHT, rather long Iberian nose with a HIGH bridge, large, dark-brown eyes under LOW, nearly STRAIGHT dark brows, smooth, flat cheeks, a full, grave mouth; dark-chestnut hair braided and pinned up under the veil; the gaze level and fearless, toward us. OPTATUS (right): a man of about fifty-five with a ROUND, DOMED, BALD head and a SHORT, BROAD face — a BROAD, FLAT nose, small, DEEP-SET, kindly dark eyes under thick grey brows, full cheeks, a wide mouth, SLIGHTLY PROMINENT ears; a fringe of cropped grey hair and a SHORT, CURLY grey beard; the gaze turned toward Engratia.
meta.basis: No likenesses survive. The book tells Optatus and seventeen companions martyred at Saragossa under Dacian in 304, and Engratia of Portugal who fled a marriage to Saragossa, reproached Dacian and died of her torments; its engraving shows her, veiled, slipping out of her father's house. Wikipedia names her companions and gives Bartolomé Bermejo's panel of her as a crowned young noblewoman with a palm (the Spanish article's lead image). The two faces, a long, square-chinned young woman and a round, bald older man, are our choice.
